decision: Given a proof state, a proposed action and a proposed result state, is this a transition that actually occurred?  Balanced binary, chance 0.50.

permitted_but_unused.reason: carries derived step features but no state text; the citation prior and every eligibility check are computed from random/train.json directly, so it added nothing and was not opened
AST-shaped and only 1,150 transitions with no tactic text; this family needs the tactic and its premise annotations, which only LeanDojo carries.  Not opened by this environment

sealed_never_read.note: not opened, not hashed here, not sampled

train_only_filter.enforcement: arena.environments.legal_transform.build_family raises SealedSplitViolation on any step whose split is not 'train'; every emitted item's provenance.source_path is prefixed 'train:'

counts.item_stream_note: sha256 of research/env_legal/items.jsonl.gz decompressed; the gzip container embeds an mtime so the compressed file's own hash is not stable

discards.definition: attempts are counted per axis over every step; 'eligibility' means the step's shape does not match the axis at all, 'invalidity' means the recorded transition did not support an argument that the corruption is invalid and the item was thrown away rather than guessed at, 'surface' means no donor existed that keeps the surface statistics matched

shortcut_audit.protocol: predictors fitted on dev-train and scored on dev-heldout; split by theorem so a matched pair cannot straddle it; train-only source data; no model call

axes_demoted_to_the_L0_control_arm_after.violated_precondition: identifier-novelty separable at 0.777; the only textually checkable form of a precondition violation raises the action's novel-identifier count, which is structural rather than tunable
axes_demoted_to_the_L0_control_arm_after.wrong_successor: before/after token Jaccard separable at 0.644 after the one permitted repair (nearest-donor sampling replaced by a within-proof successor derangement, which removed a +80-character length tell and took the axis from 0.700 to 0.664); a state one tactic-step away simply resembles the goal state more than one two steps away, and no textual donor policy removes that
axes_demoted_to_the_L0_control_arm_after.wrong_premise_uniform: designed as a control from the outset; separable at 0.775, which is the point of a visible floor

closest_graded_axis_to_the_ceiling.warning: under the ceiling but by a small margin, and only a depth-4 tree reaches it while no single feature exceeds 0.53, which points to a lemma-identity by orientation interaction reached through premise frequency.  A sibling audit (research/environments/measurements/rewrite_direction_shortcuts.json) measured a train-fitted per-lemma direction prior at 0.793 on the same decision.  Here that adversary is weak because both orientations of the same lemma are emitted, so the prior sees mixed labels; that defence is a property of this construction and would not survive a different sampling policy.  Treat this axis as AT RISK and defer to the rewrite_direction family owner.

ground_truth.note: no item is TIER_A_VERIFIED: Lean was not run.  Every negative is invalid by a construction argument recorded per axis, and every positive is a recorded LeanDojo transition that Arena has not itself replayed.

wrong_premise_uniform.constructed_invalidity_argument: the cited declaration was replaced by an unrelated library declaration with a different full name; the recorded successor is the result of applying the original
wrong_premise_uniform.residual_risk: none material; the substitute is unrelated

wrong_premise_matched.constructed_invalidity_argument: the cited declaration was replaced by a different real declaration (distinct full name and distinct final name component, so not a namespace alias); the recorded successor is the result of applying the original
wrong_premise_matched.residual_risk: the substitute could be definitionally interchangeable at this site; the distinct final-name-component guard removes namespace aliases but not `simp`-equivalent lemmas

wrong_rewrite_direction.constructed_invalidity_argument: the recorded step rewrote the equation in one orientation, replacing occurrences of one side by the other; the opposite orientation replaces occurrences of the other side, so it cannot produce the recorded successor unless the two sides coincide
wrong_rewrite_direction.residual_risk: if the equation's two sides are syntactically identical the flip is a no-op; guarded by requiring the successor to differ from the predecessor and by discarding lemmas whose final name component is a commutativity/symmetry marker, but not eliminated

wrong_rewrite_target.constructed_invalidity_argument: in the recorded transition the original `at` target's hypothesis text changed and the substituted target's hypothesis text is byte-identical before and after; a tactic retargeted at an unchanged hypothesis cannot produce the recorded successor, and a rewrite that changes nothing is an error in Lean
wrong_rewrite_target.residual_risk: none identified beyond textual parsing error

wrong_binder.constructed_invalidity_argument: the recorded successor binds the introduced names to specific, textually distinct types in order; transposing two binder names would bind each to the other's type, which contradicts the recorded successor
wrong_binder.residual_risk: none identified beyond textual parsing error

violated_precondition.constructed_invalidity_argument: the `at` clause names a hypothesis that does not occur in the recorded before-state's local context, so the tactic cannot elaborate
violated_precondition.residual_risk: none identified beyond textual parsing error

type_incompatible_argument.constructed_invalidity_argument: two explicit arguments whose recorded local-context types are textually distinct and mention disjoint identifiers were transposed, so the application is ill-typed
type_incompatible_argument.residual_risk: the two recorded types could be definitionally equal despite textual difference and disjoint identifiers; this cannot be excluded without Lean

wrong_successor.constructed_invalidity_argument: tactic application is deterministic for a fixed environment; the recorded successor of this action at this state is a specific state, and the substituted state differs from it, so the triple is not the transition that occurred
wrong_successor.residual_risk: assumes tactic determinism for a fixed environment, which holds for the tactics kept here but is an assumption rather than a check

lean_tier_a_replay.authorisation: integrator-authorised job only; this module never invokes Lean
lean_tier_a_replay.harness: LeanDojo Dojo replay, one Dojo per theorem, tactics fed in recorded order
per_item_procedure: open a Dojo at (file_path, full_name) from the item's provenance
replay steps 0..step_index-1 with their recorded tactics to reach state_before
assert the reached state's pretty-print equals the item's state_before verbatim; on mismatch record REPLAY_DESYNC and do not promote the item
for a POSITIVE: run the item's action; promote to TIER_A_VERIFIED iff the run succeeds and the resulting pretty-print equals the item's state_after verbatim

for a NEGATIVE: run the item's action; promote to TIER_A_VERIFIED iff the run raises a LeanError/TimeoutError, or succeeds with a pretty-print differing from the item's state_after; if it succeeds and matches, the constructed negative was WRONG -- record CONSTRUCTED_NEGATIVE_REFUTED and drop the item and audit its axis

budget.implication: expect ~32% of attempted items to reach TIER_A; a 1,000-item Tier-A tier therefore needs ~3,100 attempted replays
budget.wall_clock_estimate: at ~20 s/theorem with 4 workers, ~3,100 items across ~900 theorems is roughly 1.3 h; this is why it is a separate job

lean_tier_a_replay.what_tier_a_would_and_would_not_establis: It would establish that the positive transition really replays and that the negative really fails or diverges.  It would NOT establish that the negative is mathematically meaningless, nor that the theorem is true, nor anything about a different Lean version.

caveats: LeanDojo annotates only premises named in the tactic SYNTAX; simp sets, typeclass instances and definitional unfolding are invisible, so premise lists are lower bounds
states are pretty-printed text, not elaborated terms; all parsing here is textual
no item in this family has been replayed in Lean; every negative is TIER_B_CONSTRUCTED
